clue.text: Just switching direction at the end for launch

indicators.note: a direction letter in the final position is swapped for its opposite, right becoming left

blocks.note: just, in the sense of fitting or right

explanation.surface: Someone is fussing that a launch went off only by changing course at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: PROPER ends in R for right; switch it to L for left and PROPEL appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch something is to send it forward with force, which is what propelling means.

clue.text: Upended indigenous people failing to finish walkabout

definitions.note: a noun here; ROAM is used as a noun, a roam or ramble

indicators.note: not reaching the end means the final letter is dropped
in a down entry, turning something upside down reads it from the bottom up

blocks.note: the indigenous people of New Zealand

explanation.surface: An aboriginal walkabout is cut short and turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: MAORI loses its last letter to give MAOR, which is then read upwards. Walkabout evokes Australia, steering away from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is a wandering journey on foot, and to roam is to wander aimlessly.

clue.text: Nobody wants a Dickens protagonist to act like a mouse

blocks.note: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations

explanation.surface: No one would want Dickens's hero to be a timid, mousy character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads as 'no one' but is the noun for an insignificant person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipsqueak is an insignificant, unimportant person, someone dismissed as a nobody.

clue.text: Raver heading off clumsy person

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is taken away

blocks.note: a raver is someone who goes clubbing

explanation.surface: A partygoer goes off, looking awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubber is an old word for a big, awkward oaf, as in landlubber.

clue.text: German arranged a locum to attend a sight problem

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words rearranged
the a after attend, taken as written and placed last

explanation.surface: A German doctor sets up a stand-in to see to someone's eye trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pair is followed by the lone a, which attends or accompanies it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucoma is an eye disease in which raised pressure damages the optic nerve and impairs vision.

clue.text: Climate threat calls for fresh Commons talks?

blocks.note: green as in new or inexperienced
to gas is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: A climate emergency prompts demands for new parliamentary debates.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commons is Britain's elected parliamentary chamber, called the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide, methane and similar emissions trap heat in the atmosphere and drive global warming.

clue.text: Skips CBS and so suffers

indicators.note: letters that suffer are knocked out of shape and come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone misses the CBS broadcast and pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: CBS is an American television network.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip, informally, is to leave hurriedly or run off without paying, as one who absconds does.

clue.text: Small bag – in public, a basket

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the a, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A little bag carried openly, like a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabas is a woman's flat work-basket or small handbag, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Clarions used in Middle East's musical mode

indicators.note: used letters are worn and knocked about, so they emerge reordered
the reworked letters go inside the next part

explanation.surface: Trumpet calls are played in an eastern musical idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor scale is a series of notes with a flattened third, one of the standard tonal modes in Western music.

clue.text: Picasso almost drowned in white, that's obvious

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off
something drowned lies submerged within something else

explanation.surface: A Picasso painting nearly lost under whitewash is plainly visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpable literally means able to be touched, so by extension clearly perceptible or evident.

clue.text: Ancient Italian, one featured in Ibsen play

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them around
a thing featured in another appears inside it

explanation.surface: An actor playing an ancient Roman role in an Ibsen drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ibsen play' looks like a title, but play is the signal to rearrange the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabines were an ancient people of central Italy, famous from the legend of the Roman abduction of their women.

clue.text: Camilla's rock band study class

definitions.note: the ’s means is: Camilla is the answer

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a sort is a kind or class

explanation.surface: Camilla's rock group is making a study of social class.
explanation.walkthrough: Camilla, wife of King Charles III, held the title Queen Consort before becoming simply Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen consort is the title of the wife of a reigning king, which Camilla held.

clue.text: Showy celebrity joining preservation body gets spoken about

indicators.note: gets here means is taken in by the next part, which goes round it

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity
the National Trust, which preserves historic buildings
oral means spoken; about tells it to go round

explanation.surface: A flashy celebrity joins a heritage charity and gets talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental is decorative rather than functional, made for display.

clue.text: Said posh person's off fish?

indicators.note: said tells us this is spoken, in an upper-class drawl

blocks.note: how a plummy English voice pronounces this word

explanation.surface: Is a toff saying the fish has gone bad?
explanation.walkthrough: Old-fashioned upper-class English speech turns 'off' into 'orf'.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept golden in ponds.

clue.text: Artillery alternative: nitrogen-filled ball

indicators.note: filled tells us something is packed inside the next part

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An alternative weapon: a ball packed with nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military weaponry, especially heavy guns and their ammunition.

clue.text: Casually object: 'short of library – extremely'

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends of the word

explanation.surface: Someone idly objects that the stock is extremely short of library books.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something casually means doing it without purpose or direction, drifting along.

clue.text: Excluded, deprived of drinking venue?

blocks.note: first meaning: barred or shut out
second, playful meaning: de- (removed from) plus barred, as if taken out of the bar

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning reading, splitting the word into a prefix meaning removed from and a pub's counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be debarred is to be formally prevented or excluded from doing something.

clue.text: Ignorant state sends tanks to capture vessel

indicators.note: to tank is to fail badly, so the letters collapse into a new order
capturing means holding something inside

explanation.surface: A rogue nation sends armoured vehicles to seize a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' reads as the noun for armoured vehicles but is a verb meaning collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is to be uninformed, so darkness is a figurative state of ignorance.

clue.text: Amalgamate a new Spice Girl?

blocks.note: first meaning: to blend or merge
second, whimsical meaning: the Spice Girls had a Mel B and a Mel C

explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls, a 1990s British pop group, included two Mels, known as Mel B and Mel C; the question mark admits the invented third.
explanation.definitionFit: To meld is to blend or merge things into a single whole.

clue.text: Preparing to burgle housing

blocks.note: first meaning: to case a joint is to look it over before a robbery
second meaning: a protective cover or shell

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a burglar eyeing a house; housing is really a mechanical enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Casing is both the slang verb form of scouting a target and the noun for an outer protective covering.

clue.text: Maybe Latin's not quite Lady Gaga dancing with nude at back of stage

indicators.note: not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes
the back of a word is its final letter
dancing letters move about and change places

explanation.surface: Lady Gaga performs naked at the rear of the stage, which isn't quite Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' seems to apply to Lady Gaga as a whole, but it trims only Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classic example of a tongue no longer spoken natively by any community.

clue.text: City in which Handel hid, eschewing all-round applause

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid, so these letters are left out
the removed word sits around the outside, split between both ends

blocks.note: taken as written; that the city also reads straight through these letters is a coincidence of the wrapped-round removal
a hand is a round of applause

explanation.surface: A city where the composer Handel went into hiding to avoid an ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: HAN at the front and D at the back together spell HAND; strip them and the city is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the major Indian city containing New Delhi, the national capital.

clue.text: Tree with lost horse

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters drop out

explanation.surface: A tree, together with a horse that went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed evenly through a darker base colour.

clue.text: Rather fusty senior gathering yarn

indicators.note: gathering means taking something in and holding it

explanation.surface: A musty old person gathering wool to knit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like knitting wool but means a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale means no longer fresh, so staler is more so, a comparative matching rather fusty.

clue.text: Casual underwear comes to brickie's aid

blocks.note: a hod is a trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A bricklayer's casual underwear comes to the rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: A brickie is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod means careless or slapdash, done without proper attention to detail.

clue.text: Pleased about welcoming international stars

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around into a new order
welcoming means letting something in

explanation.surface: Delighted to be hosting global celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pleiades, or Seven Sisters, is a bright cluster of stars in the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Ridicule eastern half of banana republic

indicators.note: on a map east is the right, so only the right-hand half is kept

blocks.note: to guy someone is to mock them

explanation.surface: Mocking a corrupt banana republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banana republic' reads as one phrase; it splits so that republic alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is an independent republic on the north coast of South America.
